text:
Maria B.: Quick sync — we need to finalize the 'breakglass' per-customer routing override flow for enterprise customers. High-level concerns: precedence vs normal routes, header-based override syntax, console UX for granting, audit trails, and quota/billing effects. Can we align here?

Jon P.: +1. My proposal: emergency header overrides have highest precedence but require an HMAC-signed token and an admin role. Example header idea: `X-RW-Override: org=org-123;route=fast-gen;ttl=3600;sig=...` Thoughts?

Lee (security): We cannot let overrides bypass quota tracking or billing. Overrides may change routing but must still count against org quota and cost center. Also require allowlist checks (by IP or role).

Priya K.: Console UX idea: an "Apply override" modal where admin picks target org, route, expiration TTL, and provides a justification. Actions should require a second confirmation if routing to Dedicated capacity. All actions create an immutable audit event with justification.

Derek S.: If an override routes traffic to Dedicated pools, that can spike committed usage & affect billing. Need an explicit billing confirmation step and opt-in from billing contact for that org. Also add a warning in the modal.

Evan D.: Devex note: we should standardize the header format and ship SDK helpers for generating signed headers. Example header serialization: `scope=org-123;route=fast-gen;ttl=3600;sig=<hmac64>`

Maria B.: Could we split: use control-plane per-org exceptions (long-lived) editable in console + a separate emergency header for breakglass (short-lived)? Header for incident ops only, console for managed exceptions.

Jon P.: Agreed. Proposed precedence: (1) emergency HMAC header override (short TTL, highest precedence), (2) control-plane per-org exceptions list (managed via console), (3) normal route matching and policy rules. Any objections?

Lee (security): Add these constraints: header must be HMAC-signed with a tenant-scoped rotating key; header tokens cannot extend TTL beyond a max (e.g., 1h); log the override type and resolved route but redact the token. Also require an allowlist for which orgs can use header overrides.

audit-bot: audit-bot: Noted. We'll need to extend the audit schema to include `override_type`, `override_actor`, `override_ttl`, and `resolved_route`. Audit entries should include a link to the console justification when present.

Priya K.: UX extras: include a "simulate resolution" button in the modal so admins can preview which route a given request would pick up given current policies — reduces accidental misrouting. Also show a prominent banner in org settings when an active override exists (TTL or permanent).

Evan D.: API debate: header vs Authorization-style bearer token. Header seems OK but let's standardize serialization (kv pairs) and provide both a raw header and an SDK helper that sets it. Also: cache invalidation — overrides must invalidate any prefix/KV cache for affected routes to avoid stale routing.

Maria B.: Action items: Jon to write RFC for precedence + HMAC header spec (due Tue), Lee to draft security checklist and key rotation policy, Priya to prototype modal + simulation, Derek to outline billing confirmation/opt-in flow, Evan to add header SDK + cache invalidation notes. I'll schedule a 30m sync Wed. :calendar:

Jon P.: I'll start the RFC in eng-platform RFCs repo and paste a link here when it's up.

Evan D.: Quick ops note — for the emergency header, we should enforce a per-org rate limit on how often it's issued and surface usage in the console (who used it, when).

Priya K.: UX final: the console exception list should support both "permanent" and "time-limited" exceptions and show history (who created/removed).

Maria B.: Perfect. Thanks everyone. I'll capture minutes and follow up with the RFC links and meeting invite. :white_check_mark:
